name: Notion
tagline: All-in-one workspace for notes, docs, and wikis
description: Notion combines notes, docs, wikis, and project management. Teams looking for simpler, cheaper, or open-source options often switch to focused alternatives.

alternatives.name: AppFlowy
alternatives.oneLiner: Open-source Notion alternative you can self-host.
alternatives.bestFor: Privacy-minded teams who want a Notion-shaped wiki they control.
alternatives.pricingNotes: OSS core free to self-host; optional paid cloud/hosted plans.

alternatives.name: AFFiNE
alternatives.oneLiner: Privacy-first workspace combining docs, whiteboards, and databases.
alternatives.bestFor: Creators who sketch and write on the same canvas.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Freemium cloud; self-host available. Paid unlocks sync/team seats.

alternatives.name: Anytype
alternatives.oneLiner: Local-first, encrypted personal knowledge base.
alternatives.bestFor: Individuals who want ownership of a personal knowledge base.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Strong free tier; paid for extra storage/backup features.

alternatives.name: Capacities
alternatives.oneLiner: Object-based note-taking built around your content types.
cons: Not a full Notion DB clone
alternatives.bestFor: Solo knowledge workers who think in types (people, projects, books).

alternatives.name: Outline
alternatives.oneLiner: Beautiful team knowledge base, self-hostable.
cons: Not a personal PKM Swiss army knife

alternatives.name: Coda

alternatives.bestFor: Ops/product teams building lightweight internal tools in docs.

name: Slack
tagline: Team messaging and collaboration hub
description: Slack dominates workplace chat. Alternatives range from open-source self-hosted servers to lighter freemium apps with better pricing for small teams.

alternatives.name: Mattermost
alternatives.oneLiner: Open-source Slack alternative for secure self-hosting.
alternatives.bestFor: Security-conscious orgs that must own chat data.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Team Edition OSS free to self-host; Enterprise/cloud paid.

alternatives.name: Rocket.Chat
alternatives.oneLiner: Fully customizable open-source team chat.
alternatives.bestFor: Teams that need internal chat plus customer messaging.
alternatives.pricingNotes: OSS community edition; paid plans for enterprise support/features.

alternatives.name: Discord
alternatives.oneLiner: Free voice + text communities popular with startups and communities.
alternatives.bestFor: Communities, gaming-adjacent teams, early startups on a budget.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free core; Nitro is personal. Server boosts optional.

alternatives.name: Element
alternatives.oneLiner: Secure messaging on the Matrix open network.
alternatives.bestFor: Privacy/open-protocol teams and decentralized orgs.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Client OSS; Element/Matrix hosting has free & paid tiers.

alternatives.name: Twist
alternatives.oneLiner: Async-first team chat designed to reduce interruptions.
cons: Not ideal for live incident chat
alternatives.bestFor: Remote teams optimizing for deep work over real-time chat.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Freemium; paid for larger teams and advanced features.

alternatives.name: Zulip
alternatives.oneLiner: Threaded open-source chat that scales for large teams.
alternatives.bestFor: Open-source communities and big async-heavy orgs.
alternatives.pricingNotes: OSS free to self-host; Zulip Cloud freemium/paid.

name: Jira
tagline: Issue tracking and agile project management

alternatives.name: Linear

alternatives.bestFor: Modern product/eng teams leaving heavyweight Jira.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free for small teams; paid per seat as you grow.

alternatives.name: Plane
alternatives.oneLiner: Open-source project management that feels like Linear + Jira.
alternatives.bestFor: Teams that want Linear-like PM without lock-in.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Open source; cloud free tier + paid plans.

alternatives.name: Taiga
alternatives.oneLiner: Open-source agile project management for scrum and kanban.
alternatives.bestFor: Agile teams wanting classic scrum without Atlassian bloat.
alternatives.pricingNotes: OSS; Taiga.io cloud has free/limited and paid options.

alternatives.name: YouTrack
alternatives.oneLiner: JetBrains issue tracker with powerful search and workflows.
alternatives.bestFor: Eng orgs already on JetBrains tools needing serious issue tracking.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free for small teams; paid as users grow. Cloud or Server.

alternatives.name: ClickUp
alternatives.oneLiner: All-in-one productivity suite replacing multiple PM tools.
alternatives.bestFor: Teams consolidating PM + docs on one platform.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Freemium; paid seats unlock limits and advanced features.

name: Salesforce
tagline: Enterprise customer relationship management
description: Salesforce is powerful but expensive and complex. SMBs often migrate to simpler CRMs or open-source options.

quickPicks.useCase: Free CRM (no seat fee to start)

ossSection.heading: Open-source Salesforce alternatives
ossSection.intro: Want a CRM you can self-host instead of Salesforce seats? Twenty aims at a modern Salesforce-inspired experience; EspoCRM is a mature open-source CRM with extensible entities. Neither is a Salesforce clone — match your sales motion and admin capacity before migrating orgs.

alternatives.name: HubSpot CRM
alternatives.oneLiner: Free-forever CRM with marketing and sales suites.
alternatives.bestFor: SMBs starting CRM free and growing into inbound.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free CRM forever; Marketing/Sales hubs are paid seats.

alternatives.name: Pipedrive
alternatives.oneLiner: Sales-focused CRM built around deal pipelines.
alternatives.bestFor: Sales teams that live in deal stages, not marketing automation.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Paid per seat; trial available. No heavy free forever tier.

alternatives.name: Twenty
alternatives.oneLiner: Open-source CRM designed as a modern Salesforce alternative.
alternatives.bestFor: Startups wanting a modern CRM they can fork/self-host.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Open source; cloud offerings emerging — check current plans.

alternatives.name: EspoCRM
alternatives.oneLiner: Flexible open-source CRM you can self-host.
pros: No per-seat SaaS tax if hosted
alternatives.bestFor: SMBs with a bit of IT who hate Salesforce pricing.
alternatives.pricingNotes: OSS free; paid extensions/support and hosted options exist.

alternatives.name: Attio
alternatives.oneLiner: Flexible, data-driven CRM for startups and modern teams.
alternatives.bestFor: Startups that want a modern, relational CRM.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Freemium/paid — verify seat and enrichment pricing.

alternatives.name: Zoho CRM
alternatives.oneLiner: Affordable full-featured CRM in the Zoho suite.
cons: Interface can feel denser than newer CRMs
Best value when you also use other Zoho apps
Paid support tiers available beyond classic support
alternatives.bestFor: Cost-sensitive SMBs needing CRM + adjacent Zoho apps.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free forever (limited) + cheap paid editions vs Salesforce.

name: HubSpot
tagline: Inbound marketing, CRM, and sales platform
description: HubSpot's free tier is generous, but paid seats add up. Teams seek lighter marketing automation and open CRM stacks.

alternatives.name: Brevo
alternatives.oneLiner: Email, SMS, and CRM for growing businesses at lower cost.
pros: Transactional email (API/SMTP) and a free sales CRM included
cons: Free plan caps sending at 300 emails/day; dedicated IP only on Enterprise
Lighter inbound content tools (blog/SEO/CMS) than HubSpot
alternatives.bestFor: SMBs needing email/SMS without HubSpot prices.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free forever: 300 emails/day, up to 100,000 contacts. Paid plans priced by monthly email volume; SMS credits sold separately.

alternatives.name: ActiveCampaign
alternatives.oneLiner: Marketing automation with strong email + CRM features.
alternatives.bestFor: Marketers who need serious automations beyond basic newsletters.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Paid from low tiers; contact-based pricing — watch list growth.

alternatives.name: Mautic
alternatives.oneLiner: Open-source marketing automation you control.
cons: Steeper learning curve than hosted email tools
You manage sending infrastructure and deliverability
alternatives.bestFor: Technical teams wanting HubSpot-like automation without SaaS lock-in.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Open source and free; you pay for hosting and an email sending service, or a third-party managed Mautic host.

alternatives.name: Pipedrive
alternatives.oneLiner: Pipeline CRM that many teams use instead of HubSpot Sales.
alternatives.bestFor: Sales orgs leaving HubSpot Sales for a simpler pipeline CRM.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Paid per seat; compare annual vs monthly carefully.

alternatives.name: Close
alternatives.oneLiner: Sales CRM built for high-velocity outbound teams.
pros: Built-in calling, SMS and email on all plans, plus Chloe AI sales agent
cons: No free plan (14-day trial, no card)
alternatives.bestFor: High-velocity outbound sales teams.
alternatives.pricingNotes: From $9/user/mo (Solo, annual) to $139 (Scale). 14-day trial, no card needed; 30-day money-back. Calls and SMS billed at cost (about $0.02/min).

alternatives.name: Listmonk
alternatives.oneLiner: Self-hosted newsletter and mailing list manager.
cons: No fancy visual builder like ESPs
alternatives.bestFor: Dev-friendly teams sending newsletters they fully control.
alternatives.pricingNotes: 100% free OSS; pay only for VPS and email provider.

name: Figma
tagline: Collaborative interface design tool
description: Figma redefined design collaboration. After pricing changes, many designers explore open-source and cheaper design tools.

alternatives.name: Penpot
alternatives.oneLiner: Open-source design and prototyping platform for teams.
alternatives.bestFor: Teams wanting Figma-like collab without Adobe/Figma lock-in.
alternatives.pricingNotes: OSS free; Penpot Cloud freemium/paid.

alternatives.name: Sketch
alternatives.oneLiner: Mac-native UI design tool with strong plugin ecosystem.
alternatives.bestFor: Mac-centric design teams okay without browser-first multiplayer.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Paid subscription (individual/team). No free forever.

alternatives.name: Framer
alternatives.oneLiner: Design and ship production websites in one tool.
cons: Not a full UI-system design tool
alternatives.bestFor: Designers shipping marketing sites without a separate handoff.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Freemium; paid for custom domains, CMS, team features.

alternatives.name: Lunacy
alternatives.oneLiner: Free design tool with offline support and built-in assets.
alternatives.bestFor: Individuals needing a free design tool with asset packs.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free tier generous; cloud/team features may be paid.

alternatives.name: Pencil
alternatives.oneLiner: Open-source prototyping tool focused on speed.
alternatives.bestFor: Solo designers prototyping wireframes offline.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free OSS desktop app.

alternatives.name: Adobe XD
alternatives.oneLiner: Adobe's UI/UX design and prototyping app.
alternatives.bestFor: Teams already deep in Creative Cloud who must stay there.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Via Adobe CC plans — often bundled, not best standalone value.

name: Zendesk
tagline: Customer support and ticketing platform
description: Zendesk is the enterprise helpdesk standard. Growing teams often switch to an open source Zendesk alternative they can self-host, or a simpler SMB SaaS desk.

alternatives.name: Freshdesk
alternatives.oneLiner: Affordable helpdesk with omnichannel support.
pros: Ticketing, shared inbox, knowledge base and customer portal on every plan
cons: AI Agent sessions beyond the first 500 are a paid add-on ($49 per 100)
Skill-based routing, sandbox and audit logs are Enterprise-only
alternatives.bestFor: SMBs needing tickets without Zendesk enterprise pricing.
alternatives.pricingNotes: 14-day free trial; Growth from $19/agent/mo billed annually (Pro $55, Enterprise $89). A 2-agent Free Program is available in-app for 6 months.

alternatives.name: Chatwoot
alternatives.oneLiner: Open-source customer engagement suite.
cons: Enterprise controls often need paid Cloud or EE
alternatives.bestFor: Teams wanting an open Intercom/Zendesk-lite stack.
alternatives.pricingNotes: MIT Community Edition free to self-host. Chatwoot Cloud: Hacker $0 (2 agents); Startups $19, Business $39, Enterprise $99 per agent/mo billed annually.

alternatives.name: FreeScout
alternatives.oneLiner: Lightweight open-source help desk and shared inbox.
alternatives.bestFor: Small support teams wanting a simple open help desk.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free OSS; optional paid modules from FreeScout.

alternatives.name: Help Scout
alternatives.oneLiner: Human-friendly shared inbox for customer support.
cons: Paid per user beyond the free tier
AI Answers is a metered add-on
alternatives.bestFor: Customer-centric SMBs that hate cluttered agent UIs.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free up to 5 users. Annual: Standard $25, Plus $45, Pro $75 per user/mo. AI Answers ~$0.75 per resolution.

alternatives.name: Intercom
alternatives.oneLiner: Conversational support and customer messaging platform.
cons: Premium pricing vs classic helpdesk tools
More chat/product-messaging oriented than ticket queues
Plan options take time to map to seat counts
alternatives.bestFor: SaaS products mixing support chat with lifecycle messaging.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Paid platforms — expect significant monthly spend vs Zendesk SMB.

alternatives.name: Gorgias
alternatives.oneLiner: Helpdesk built for ecommerce brands.
alternatives.bestFor: DTC/ecommerce brands on Shopify-like stacks.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Paid by ticket volume tiers — model cost on peak season.

alternatives.name: Baserow
alternatives.oneLiner: No-code database, open-source and self-hostable.
cons: Self-host maintenance if you go that route
alternatives.bestFor: Ops teams wanting Airtable-like grids they can host.

alternatives.oneLiner: Managed app hosting on DigitalOcean with predictable container pricing.
pros: Ties into Droplets, Spaces, and managed DBs
Simple PaaS path if you already know DigitalOcean
cons: Fewer niche platform add-ons than Render's catalog
alternatives.bestFor: Teams already on DigitalOcean wanting Render-like deploys at predictable cost.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Static sites free (limited); shared containers from $5/mo; dedicated plans from ~$29/mo.

alternatives.name: Vultr
alternatives.oneLiner: Cloud VPS and managed services when you prefer servers over a full PaaS.
pros: Cloud Compute from about $2.50–$5/mo depending on IPv4/IPv6 and size
Hourly billing with bandwidth included on plans
Pair with Coolify for a self-hosted PaaS UX
cons: Not a PaaS by itself — you manage the OS (or add Coolify)
Automatic backups add ~20% to instance price
Managed databases are a separate product
alternatives.bestFor: Teams comfortable with Linux who want cheaper-than-Render compute.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Regular Performance from ~$2.50/mo (IPv6-only) / higher with IPv4; High Performance from ~$6/mo. Backups +20%. Prices vary by region.

alternatives.name: Fly.io
alternatives.oneLiner: Run containers close to users on a global edge network.
pros: Global edge placement for lower latency
cons: More ops than classic Render/Heroku PaaS
Learning flyctl and networking takes time
Watch usage-based billing on egress and machines
alternatives.bestFor: Teams that outgrew single-region PaaS and need global containers.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Usage-based; free allowances vary — check current Fly.io Free tier.

alternatives.name: Coolify
alternatives.oneLiner: Self-hosted Heroku/Vercel-like PaaS on your own VPS.
pros: Self-host full PaaS UX on a cheap VPS
Deploy many apps without per-dyno vendor tax
cons: You manage the server and updates
HA and backups are your responsibility
alternatives.bestFor: DevOps-comfortable teams escaping Render bills with a VPS + PaaS UI.
alternatives.pricingNotes: OSS free; Coolify Cloud optional. Run on a VPS (e.g. Vultr or DigitalOcean).

name: ActiveCampaign
tagline: Marketing automation with email, CRM-style contacts, and AI assists
description: ActiveCampaign is a full marketing automation suite. Teams looking for ActiveCampaign alternatives — or something cheaper than ActiveCampaign — often switch to simpler ESPs, creator newsletter platforms, or HubSpot Marketing when seat and contact costs climb.

alternatives.name: MailerLite
alternatives.oneLiner: Simple email marketing and automations that stay affordable as lists grow.
pros: Comfort from $12/mo (500 subscribers) — often cheaper than ActiveCampaign Starter
Campaigns, automations, landing pages, and forms included
Free plan to try: 250 subscribers / 2,500 emails/mo
cons: Fewer deep CRM / multi-channel features than ActiveCampaign Plus+
alternatives.bestFor: SMBs and creators who want cheaper-than-ActiveCampaign email automation.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free: 250 subs / 2,500 emails/mo. Comfort from $12/mo, Power from $25/mo (500-subscriber tier).

alternatives.name: beehiiv
alternatives.oneLiner: Newsletter-first platform with growth and monetization tools.
pros: Free up to 2,500 subscribers with unlimited sends
Built for audience growth (referrals, ads, web)
cons: Not a full ActiveCampaign-style marketing automation + CRM suite
Automations and monetization features need Lite+
No SMS or deep sales CRM
alternatives.bestFor: Publishers and creators who need newsletters more than enterprise automation.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free up to 2,500 subs. Lite from $49/mo, Pro from $95/mo (yearly, 1,000-sub tier).

alternatives.name: Brevo
alternatives.oneLiner: Email + SMS marketing priced by sends, with a generous free tier.
pros: Email and SMS under one roof
Free forever: 300 emails/day, up to 100,000 contacts stored
Priced mainly by email volume, not contacts stored
cons: Phone support only on higher paid plans
Free/Starter automation contact caps (unlimited from Standard)
alternatives.bestFor: Teams leaving ActiveCampaign for send-based pricing and SMS.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free: 300 emails/day. Paid plans by monthly email volume; SMS credits separate.

alternatives.name: Kit (ConvertKit)
alternatives.oneLiner: Creator email marketing with tagging, sequences, and digital products.
cons: Visual automations need paid Creator plan
Email-first — not a full B2B marketing automation stack
Subscriber-tier pricing steps up as you grow
alternatives.bestFor: Creators who find ActiveCampaign heavier than they need.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free up to 10,000 subscribers. Creator automations from $39/mo at 1,000 subscribers.

alternatives.name: HubSpot Marketing Hub
alternatives.oneLiner: Marketing automation inside the HubSpot CRM ecosystem.
pros: Free CRM foundation; Marketing Hub adds email and automation
cons: Marketing Hub paid seats/contacts can exceed simpler ESPs at scale
Feature gates between Free, Starter, and Professional
Can feel complex if you only need newsletters
alternatives.bestFor: Teams already on HubSpot CRM who want marketing automation in one vendor.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free CRM tools available. Marketing Hub Starter and above are paid — confirm current HubSpot pricing for your contact band.

name: Coda
tagline: Doc-database hybrid (now Superhuman Docs) for team wikis and apps
description: Coda (rebranding toward Superhuman Docs) blends docs with tables and automations. Teams looking for Coda alternatives — especially Coda alternatives for small teams — often want Airtable-like bases, Notion docs, or open-source grids without Doc Maker pricing.

alternatives.name: Teable
alternatives.oneLiner: Fast open-source Airtable-like database on Postgres.
pros: Cloud Free plan plus self-host OSS path
AI fields/chat available; Pro from about $13/seat/mo yearly
cons: Newer than Notion or Airtable — templates still growing
Cloud Free has row/storage limits (e.g. ~1,000 rows/space)
Less 'doc canvas' than classic Coda pages
alternatives.bestFor: Small teams who want Coda-like structured data with an Airtable feel and OSS option.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Cloud Free $0 (limited rows/storage). Pro ~$13/seat/mo yearly, Business ~$20/seat/mo yearly. Self-host OSS available.

alternatives.name: Notion
alternatives.oneLiner: All-in-one docs, wikis, and databases most teams already know.
pros: Free plan strong for individuals and small teams
cons: Databases are not a full relational DB
Perf can dip on very large bases
Fewer 'Pack-like' live syncs than Coda's strongest packs
alternatives.bestFor: Teams who want Coda-style docs without learning a new doc-maker model.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free / Plus / Business seat plans — confirm current Notion pricing for your team size.

alternatives.name: Airtable
alternatives.oneLiner: Spreadsheet-database hybrid with views, interfaces, and automations.
pros: Familiar for ops and product teams
cons: Seat and record limits push teams to paid plans
Less freeform long-form docs than Coda/Notion
Can get expensive as collaborators grow
alternatives.bestFor: Teams that outgrew Coda tables and want a dedicated database UX.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Freemium; Team/Business priced per collaborator — check current Airtable plans.

alternatives.name: NocoDB
alternatives.oneLiner: Open-source Airtable alternative on top of your SQL database.
pros: Airtable-like UI on Postgres/MySQL you own
OSS self-host — no per-row SaaS tax
Cloud option if you skip ops
cons: Self-host means you manage the SQL database
Fewer polished doc/page features than Coda
Cloud free tier caps records and editors
alternatives.bestFor: Technical small teams wanting Coda/Airtable structure with data ownership.
alternatives.pricingNotes: OSS free to self-host. NocoDB Cloud Free limited; paid Plus from about $12/editor/mo annual.

alternatives.name: Craft
alternatives.oneLiner: Beautiful docs and notes with a strong writing-first UX.
pros: Good for handbooks and narrative docs
cons: Not an Airtable-strength database — weaker relational tables than Coda/Teable
Team plan is a bigger jump than solo Plus
Smaller automation ecosystem than Coda Packs
alternatives.bestFor: Writers and small teams who loved Coda's docs more than its databases.
alternatives.pricingNotes: Free/Starter with limits; Plus about $8/mo yearly ($10 monthly); Team plans for multi-seat.
